title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：turkey　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 turkey 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the cook ① cooked the turkey that no guest in the canteen would have described, and he said the cooking was the whole of the day. The ② turkey, meaning the bird itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed undescribed in the book; a turkey, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ turkey in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ turkey at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A turkey, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the cook said the describing is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the turkey was the whole of the matter, meaning the feast and not the bird. The ⑥ turkey, meaning the feast and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; turkey, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both a bird and a feast. He said the feast is the part they remember.

By 1983 the ⑦ turkey had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ turkey of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of describing; turkey, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ turkey I remember is the bird described in the menu, which closed in 1985 and is still described as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ turkey, my mother said in 1987, is the only bird that improves by being described; every turkey, she said, is a feast that has agreed to look like a bird. She said the feast was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 火鸡（指食堂里每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 火鸡（指那只火鸡本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook the turkey 烤这一只火鸡
D. n. 火鸡（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 火鸡之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的火鸡之事）
F. n. 火鸡（指菜单里写到、被描述的那一只）
G. n. 火鸡、节庆（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 节庆（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: cook the turkey 意为“烤这一只火鸡”，1978 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯描述的一只火鸡做了一遍。
turkey 意为“火鸡”，指那只火鸡本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被描述。
turkey 意为“火鸡”，指食堂里每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
turkey 意为“火鸡”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
turkey 意为“火鸡、节庆”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这只节庆就是那件事的全部。
turkey 意为“节庆”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那只火鸡，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
turkey 意为“火鸡”，指菜单里写到、被描述的那一只，到 1983 年这一只成了菜单里的一行。
turkey 意为“火鸡之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的火鸡之事是一处食堂和三个日子的描述。
turkey 意为“火鸡”，我记得的是菜单里描述过的那一只，1985 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一只。
turkey 为抽象总称，母亲 1987 年说，火鸡是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的火鸡。
